prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1466; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant regarding a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Claimant reports stopping at a red light when their vehicle was struck from behind. Reports neck strain and stiffness, treated at urgent care the same day. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Liability appears clear based on initial description. Opened file and requested the police report number.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. Responding officer documented the other driver's statement that they looked away from the road briefly. Both vehicles drivable from scene, no airbag deployment noted. Photos of both vehicles received from claimant and reviewed. Damage to rear bumper and trunk area on claimant's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact. Estimate requested from preferred body shop.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant to confirm medical treatment details. Urgent care records received, showing diagnosis of cervical strain with prescribed muscle relaxants and a recommendation for physical therapy. Claimant asked what the claims process involves and whether they need to hire a lawyer. Explained that they are free to choose representation and that I can only provide information about our process, not legal advice. Claimant said they will think about it.

Entry 4: Repair estimate received and reviewed. Shop reports parts are on order and estimated repair time is about two weeks. Rental vehicle coverage confirmed under claimant's policy and rental arranged. Claimant reports neck pain is ongoing but improving. Physical therapy appointments scheduled. Requested itemized medical bills and records from the treating provider.

Entry 5: Medical records and first bill received. Reviewed for consistency with reported injury and treatment dates. No prior claims found on claimant's history in the database. Sent written update to the claimant describing next steps, including the expected timeline for the injury evaluation. Set diary reminder to follow up after physical therapy progress notes arrive.
